misclassified_entities.reason: Internal component - Provider state change is an internal event trigger within the provider, not an external entity

trusted_external_entities.name: Calling Contract (Identity Precompile)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Smart contract invoking the identity precompile via CALL. May pass untrusted data through identity for memory operations. All input data treated as arbitrary bytes.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet Provider (SHADOW Protocol)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External wallet application that has registered a web+evm:// protocol handler. Protocol handler registration requires user installation, implying some trust, but message content still requires origin validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blockchain Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Underlying blockchain network(s) the provider connects to. Network reachability is untrusted - connection state must be properly tracked and events emitted.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet Browser Extension
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Browser extension that injects the Ethereum provider into web pages. User explicitly installed the extension, granting implicit trust. However, a malicious extension could emit false events.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Web application that consumes the Ethereum provider API. Attaches event listeners to the provider. Should not be trusted with sensitive operations without user consent.

trusted_external_entities.name: Web User (Block Explorer)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External user or application requesting blockchain data via standardized explorer URLs. URL path parameters are untrusted input requiring validation to prevent injection attacks.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Identity precompile echoes data without modification. Gas validation ensures caller paid for data size. No content validation performed - all bytes pass through unchanged.
Wallet responds via protocol handler with MessagePort for communication. First port becomes primary channel. Origin verification required for all subsequent messages.
All wallet messages must pass origin validation. Response must contain exactly one of result or error. Invalid responses rejected.
ProviderInfo must contain valid name and icon fields. Icon URI should be validated before rendering to prevent XSS via malicious icon URLs.
Network connectivity is transient and may be lost at any time. Chain ID should match eth_chainId when RPC is operational. Connect events must be emitted to all listeners.
All network connections may be lost simultaneously. Disconnect events must be emitted when no chains are reachable. DApps must handle disconnection gracefully.
Provider injection implies user has installed and trusts the wallet extension. However, multiple conflicting providers may exist. User may not understand full security implications.
DApp listener callbacks may throw exceptions. Provider must handle listener errors without affecting other listeners. Invocation order is not guaranteed.
URL path is untrusted input. Must validate against expected patterns (/block/*, /tx/*, /address/*, /token/*). Identifiers must be validated for format before database queries.
Block hash/height, tx hash, and address parameters must be validated to prevent path traversal, SQL injection, or XSS. Invalid identifiers should return 404.
